stemMd: A general price index rises from 100 to 110 while a household's nominal income remains unchanged. What happens to that income's purchasing power relative to the indexed basket?

options.label: E
options.textMd: It remains unchanged because the income number is constant.

explanationMd: The same nominal income buys fewer units of a basket that now costs more. Its purchasing power falls to 100/110 of the previous amount, about 90.9%. Nominal stability does not imply real stability.

distractorRationale.d: Higher prices reduce what fixed income buys.
distractorRationale.a: The price change does not double income.
distractorRationale.e: Real purchasing power depends on prices as well as nominal income.
distractorRationale.b: A ten-percent price rise does not eliminate all buying power.
